newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy slowly recovering despite weakness.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy slowly recovering despite weakness.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to show a gradual improvement but the recovery is patchy and needs the continued spur of easy credit, the government said on Friday.

In a regular report on the health of the economy, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) stuck to its previous view that the economy is gradually recovering but added a negative note, saying there were some elements of weakness.
"No one feels that the economy is rapidly recovering, but nor are there bad or worsening factors to worry about," an EPA official told reporters.

There has been some concern in Japan's financial markets, triggered by weak data recently, that the nation's tentative recovery from the slump which followed the 1980s "bubble" era may have ground to a halt.
The EPA monthly report also prescribed the same remedies as before -- deregulation, expansion of domestic demand and a continued easy credit policy by the Bank of Japan.
The central bank chief echoed the view that the recovery was still gradual and said the Bank of Japan would continue to seek a stronger improvement.
"The Bank of Japan's monetary policy will continue to be geared to making a firmer basis for economic recovery," BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita told a meeting of business executives on Friday.

The central bank has held Japan's key interest rate, the official discount rate, at a record low of 0.5 percent for just over a year to keep the recovery alive and allow it to gather strength. The Bank of Japan charges this rate on certain loans to commercial banks.
The EPA official singled out household spending as the main factor prompting the EPA to strike a note of caution in its assessment of the economy.
Household spending, considered a barometer of the strength of private consumption, fell 4.4 percent in July from a year earlier to an average 326,257 yen ($2,936) per household.
But the official was quick to add that temporary elements, such as a food poisoning epidemic that swept Japan this summer, contributed to the slack spending in July.
"There's no significant change in the content of the report," said Satoshi Shimamoto, senior economist at MMS International in Tokyo.
The wording of the report is scrutinised by markets for signs of any shift in confidence that would have a bearing on interest rate policy.
"Moderate recovery, or gradual recovery, has several stages and what the EPA has done is come down one notch of that range," said Aaron Cohen, senior economist at Daiwa Securities.
The EPA official said the report maintains that the basic trend in private consumption continues to be one of gradual recovery, and that private demand remains steady.
The official cited a rise in department store sales and sales of durable goods, as well as increased personal income, as other positive factors fostering gradual recovery in personal spending.
As for factors which support a gradual increase in production, the report pointed to bright signs in capital spending and housing construction.
The government declared in February that the nation's economy had finally started to recover. But the EPA has not been able to take its assessment further than a "gradual recovery" since then.
